title: Google Workspace Security Baseline, DLP & Context-Aware Access (CAA)
author_notes: Effort tier: T4 (Google Workspace + Gemini enterprise transformation; architecture/governance/integration or migration work, live-environment care).

Google Admin console + Microsoft/Entra authored click-by-click from public docs; Gemini Enterprise preview/rolling-out capabilities cited or flagged 'verify in tenant', never invented; third-party migration-tool and enterprise-app internals deferred to vendor docs.
hook: Harden Google Workspace to enterprise standard from day one
problem: A new Google Workspace tenant is not secure by default at enterprise standard. This solution establishes the Google Workspace security posture: an admin-console hardening baseline (2SV, session controls, sharing), Data Loss Prevention (DLP) rules for Drive/Gmail, and Context-Aware Access (CAA) that gates access on device and context — so corporate data is protected under Zero-Trust, deployed pilot-first and rollback-ready.
whats_inside: Solution Overview — the Workspace security model: hardening baseline, DLP, Context-Aware Access, and how they enforce Zero-Trust.
Requirements Guide — prerequisites (Workspace edition supporting DLP/CAA, super-admin, identity/context signals, a pilot OU) with how to verify/implement each.
Implementation Guide — exact steps to apply the named hardening baseline (2SV, sessions, sharing), build DLP rules for Drive/Gmail, and define CAA access levels + assignments, on a pilot then expand.
5 supporting scripts — security-posture discovery, per-OU baseline/DLP/CAA validation, a posture coverage/exception report, safe remediation, and a scope helper.
Testing & Troubleshooting Guides (baseline applied, DLP blocks, CAA gates) plus Best Practices for staged enforcement.
short: Establish the Google Workspace security posture — admin hardening baseline, DLP for Drive/Gmail, and Context-Aware Access — so corporate data is protected under Zero-Trust, pilot-first. Self-guided, tested, a fraction of consulting cost.
